summary: WDAC policy hash mismatch after imaging prevents smartcard & corporate SSO logon on several device models
description:
Issue summary: After routine depot-repair imaging we are seeing Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy hash mismatches on boot for a subset of devices. Affected machines drop the corporate SSO/Netlogon smartcard auth path and fall back to local credential screens, which blocks automated post-imaging enrollment tasks (Intune/AAD join) and prevents users from completing first-login flows.

Impact: Affected users cannot complete provisioning during first sign-in; automated device configuration (policies, cert enrollment, company portal) does not complete. This impacts onboarding for employees receiving repaired machines and delays returns to service. Estimated ~6-9% of depot-imaged devices from last week's imaging bundle.

Environment: Production fleet (depot repair image) in us-east and eu-west regions. Primary models observed: Dell Latitude 5430, Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen11. Imaging performed via SCCM task sequence (corp-imaging-v3.4) with post-image WDAC registration step.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Re-image device using SCCM task sequence corp-imaging-v3.4 with WDAC policy package applied.
2) Complete OOBE and network join steps.
3) Sign in with corporate SSO (smartcard or Windows Hello for Business).
4) Observe that Windows shows WDAC hash mismatch event and LSA/Winlogon rejects enterprise authentication flows.

Observed behavior: WinEvent shows WDAC Policy Integrity Error (Event ID 799) during early logon; LSA reports Smartcard logon path disabled due to code integrity failure; Intune device check-in stalls and never reaches "Compliant" state. Devices sometimes prompt for BitLocker recovery on first resume.

Expected behavior: WDAC policy should validate against the policy catalog shipped in the image; post-image registration should succeed, allowing SSO and Intune enrollment to complete without manual intervention.

Relevant logs & artifacts:
- C:\Windows\System32\winevt\Logs\Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity%4Operational.evtx shows Event 799 and code integrity hash mismatch entries.
- SCCM task sequence smsts.log entries show WDAC registration step completing with exit code 0 on some machines but event mismatch on others.
- USB-attached smartcard readers show driver load sequences in SetupAPI logs that overlap with policy registration on affected devices.

Temporary workaround: In depot, imaging techs can skip the WDAC registration step and instead stage a follow-up script that runs after first user login to register the WDAC policy (delays enforcement until authentication subsystems are fully initialized). This allows Intune enrollment to complete.

Notes: This appears correlated with a FW revision in the NVMe controller and a changed driver load timing on a subset of inventory. Hypothesis is a timing window between WDAC policy application and device driver signature validation leading to a transient policy hash recalculation.

resolution: Workaround implemented: Imaging team created corp-imaging-v3.4a which defers WDAC registration until after first-user login, allowing Intune/AAD join to complete. Depot technicians updated runbook and were instructed to apply deferred-registration variant for affected models. Long-term fix: Security and Endpoint Eng to coordinate with NVMe vendor and WDAC maintainers to ensure deterministic policy application; plan to update the task sequence to include a driver-init wait-step or registry flag to stabilize hash calculation. Follow-up ticket planned for FW/vendor engagement and permanent task-sequence change.
root_cause_analysis: Preliminary RCA: A timing-dependent interaction between NVMe controller driver initialization (newer FW) and the WDAC policy registration step in the imaging sequence caused a non-deterministic recalculation of the policy/runtime hash. When the runtime hash differs at early boot, the code integrity subsystem rejects enterprise authentication paths until policy is re-registered under stable driver load ordering.
workaround_steps: 1) Use corp-imaging-v3.4a (deferred WDAC) in depot for Dell 5430 and X1 Carbon Gen11 until permanent fix is deployed.

2) If device is already affected, have depot tech login with local admin, run: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\scripts\deferred-wdac-register.ps1" to register the policy post-login and reboot.
3) If smartcard authentication still fails, escalate to Security with collected EventLog bundle (CodeIntegrity, System, SetupAPI).
